log.why: Test the leading candidate hisG directly; a positive result will strongly confirm it in a single plate.
Testing at 3 µM bisects the prior probability mass (0.616 <= 3 µM vs 0.384 > 3 µM) for maximum information gain.
E4 splits the posterior probability mass evenly (0.523 vs 0.477) around 10 µM, and can incubate while we publish Ticket 1.
E9 splits the prior probability mass nearly in half (0.464 vs 0.536) for maximum information gain on Ticket 3.
Test the leading candidate sodA (0.390) on Ticket 3 so it can incubate while we handle other tickets.
hisG has a strong 0.856 posterior after E1 lost the phenotype, making immediate publication optimal to secure points and open a ticket slot.
Test top candidate katG (0.561) against second candidate gyrA (0.242) while utilizing a free incubator.
With 10 µM at 0.646 posterior and time running low, publishing now secures good points and frees bench time for other tickets.
Ticket 3 is urgent (35s left) and knocking out gyrA directly tests the leading hypothesis (0.484 posterior).
Test {rpoB, ftsZ} on Ticket 4 to split the prior probability mass nearly in half while Ticket 3 incubates.
Ticket 3 is about to expire in 8s; publishing recA at 0.264 has higher expected value (-12) than letting it expire (-30).
Ticket 4 expires soon; testing the leading candidate katG (0.457) directly will either confirm it or leave lacZ as the leader before publishing.
Test 1 uM on Ticket 5 to split the probability mass nearly in half while waiting for Ticket 4's E4 result.
E3 at 3 uM best distinguishes the leading hypothesis (3 uM, 0.461) from higher dose thresholds like 10 uM (0.233).
Testing top candidate dnaK on Ticket 7 while waiting for Ticket 5's E3 plate, leaving time to publish both.
Round is ending in 3 seconds and dnaK has a high posterior of 0.846 after losing the phenotype in E2.
